pronunciation_notes.text: Č is pronounced as 'chuh', similar to the pronunciation of 'c' in Woccon.
pronunciation_notes.source_excerpt: Siouan languages usually use Americanist Phoenetic languages. Č=chuh, but so does our “c”

pronunciation_notes.text: Vowel pronunciation: E is represented by the letter I (i pronounced like an e), U is pronounced like oo, A can be ay or ah, O is oh.
pronunciation_notes.source_excerpt: E= represented by letter I (i=pronounced like an e) U=pronounced like oo A=ay and ah O=oh

pronunciation_notes.text: Vowel length: Short vowels are pronounced for a short time, often represented with two vowels in English. Long sounds are written with a colon (:).
pronunciation_notes.source_excerpt: 4 short vowels= spend short time on them, often in English they are represented with two vowels Long sounds are often written with a colon (:) I=e e=ay a=ah u-=oo
